checks.name: absolute-path-closed-allowlist-and-no-home
checks.summary: all deterministic and starting no process. The executable must be absolute, its filepath.Base must equal git and it must stat to a regular file: a relative path, a traversal path, a wrong basename, a lookalike basename, an absent file, a directory and a symlink are each refused, through an injected Stat hook that touches no filesystem, with a positive control that a valid path is accepted. The subcommand allowlist is asserted to be exactly the fourteen declared entries, to contain none of push, fetch, remote, submodule, config, credential or worktree, and to be what refuses each of them (allowedGitSubcommand is the allowlist's only reader and buildGitArgv its only caller); a non-test file naming one of those subcommands as a string literal is also refused by an AST scan. The built argv carries -C with the absolute working copy root, because ProcessSupervisor has no Dir field. The child environment's names are exactly PATH, GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL, GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM and GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT with the two config scopes pinned to /dev/null; HOME is absent from the environment AND absent from the allowlist, and HOME, GIT_SSH_COMMAND, GIT_ASKPASS and SSH_AUTH_SOCK are each refused when a caller tries to add them, while the two commit-only date names are accepted.

checks.name: real-git-real-namespace-real-refusals
checks.summary: PASS in 0.40s. Nothing faked: the real git binary at the absolute path above, a real rootless user+mount namespace from the real unshare, and the kernel's own refusals. Measured, in order: a bare origin created at test time in t.TempDir() by the real git binary (built by cloning a seed working tree with --bare, so no push and no ref anywhere); clone --no-hardlinks into <workspace_root>/execution-1/source inside the namespace; git rev-parse --git-common-dir == ".git" and .git is a DIRECTORY, proving an independent repository rather than a linked worktree; the descriptor beside the copy naming increment_id, execution_id, repository_id and created_at; branch loop/increment-1 created; a two-file ChangeSet applied and staged; the pre-change observation clean with zero changed paths, the staged observation not clean; commit; the post-commit observation clean, on the change branch, with head and tree matching the commit, HEAD advanced off the base, the base commit preserved and changed_paths == 2; project-level verification refused with ErrProjectVerificationNotWired. Then the confined writes: into the sealed top-level ancestor REFUSED, into the origin directory REFUSED, into a SIBLING Execution's workspace REFUSED, and in each case no file was created; a write inside the Execution's own workspace SUCCEEDED, so the refusals are about location and not about writing. Finally a hand-built git push to the file-path origin inside the confinement was REFUSED and left no ref in the origin -- that argv had to be built by hand precisely because the adapter cannot construct it. Discard removed the copy and is idempotent. Logged as execution facts: the resolved absolute git path, git version 2.55.0, the kernel release, the workspace root, and the sealed top-level ancestor /tmp.

checks.name: lifetime-and-deterministic-sweep
checks.summary: both PASS. Lifetime: two Executions of the SAME Increment get separate clones at their own paths, no directory keyed by the increment id alone is created, re-materialising over an existing copy is refused with ErrWorkingCopyExists rather than reusing it, and a commit in one copy is not visible in the other. Sweep: two copies are made, a FRESHLY constructed provider over the same workspace root (the state a Runner restarting after a crash is in) sweeps with only one id active, exactly the inactive tree is removed, the active copy is still present AND still verifies on its branch, the origin's refs are byte-identical before and after by both rev-parse --all and for-each-ref, and a second sweep is a no-op. No goroutine, no sleep and no timer anywhere in the file: ProcessSupervisor.Run is synchronous, so every step is ordered by its return. A separate deterministic test proves the sweep leaves a symlink child alone, never follows it outside the root, and that Discard refuses an execution id that is empty, "..", nested or absolute.
